binders: Universally quantify v = valueAtJump over all real numbers.
The function q_v has two real arguments, spatial coordinate x and time t, and takes real values.
In the first integrability assertion, universally quantify a,b,t over Real.
In the second integrability assertion, universally quantify x,s,t over Real.
In the integral balance identity, universally quantify a,b,s,t over Real, independently and without order restrictions.

Inside the negated pointwise property, qt and qx are existentially quantified real derivative values for the fixed v, position 0, and time 1. The qx existential is nested under qt, and both witnesses must satisfy the same conjunction.
In the final assertion, universally quantify the candidate derivative d over Real, inside the quantification over v.
Variables x and τ inside integrals, and variables ξ and τ inside derivative slices, are bound real arguments.
hypotheses: There are no propositional hypotheses on v.
The ambient structures are the real field with its usual norm and topology and the fixed measure μ selected as Real.measureSpace.volume.
conclusions: For every a,b,t ∈ ℝ, the function x ↦ q_v(x,t) is μ-integrable on both (a,b] and (b,a].
For every x,s,t ∈ ℝ, the function τ ↦ q_v(x,τ) is μ-integrable on both (s,t] and (t,s].
For every a,b,s,t ∈ ℝ, ∫_a^b q_v(x,t) dμ(x) − ∫_a^b q_v(x,s) dμ(x) = ∫_s^t [q_v(a,τ) − q_v(b,τ)] dμ(τ), where all integrals are oriented interval integrals.
